The test contains effectively one assertion per execution path (either assertNull in the try or assertTrue on the exception message in the catch). It does not comprehensively assert multiple properties of the returned object/state (only null-or-exception is checked), so it may miss subtler faults.

No @Ignore or @Disabled annotations are present in the provided method. There are no commented-out @Test annotations or commented-out test code within the method; the test appears active and runnable.
The class-level Javadoc contains 'Requirement trace: HEAP-REQ-001', providing explicit linkage between the test and a requirement. This constitutes traceability information for the test.

practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API methods (newHeap, copia, retiraMax) and does not use reflection or inspect internal state. There are no indications of coupling to implementation internals, suggesting good maintainability practices.

Assertions include descriptive failure messages (assertNull and assertTrue both include messages). The test uses specific assertions (assertNull and assertTrue with message) rather than only generic assertTrue without context, meeting the practice’s criteria.

The test includes concise Given-When-Then comments that explain the test intent (why the setup is performed and what is expected). There is no commented-out code or excessive noisy comments, so comments are appropriate and helpful.

The test does not use random number generators, system time, sleeps, or external dependencies directly. It relies on deterministic setup (newHeap with a fixed parameter) and local variables, so results are deterministic given the same environment.
